description: Solo team led by Milena Zarkova, an independent researcher and inventor from Bulgaria specializing in cybernetics, thermodynamics, and holistic systems design. I am working independently on a pre-developed feedforward method for preventive fire immunity and thermal homeostasis in microgravity. The team is complete and not looking for additional members.
summary: Traditional fire suppression systems in space and on Earth operate reactively—they wait for a fire to ignite, failing against invisible "cool flames" (200°C–300°C) in microgravity or destroying priceless assets with water and chemicals.  "The Argon Loop" introduces a cybernetic feedforward method that pre-programs the atmosphere itself using a breathable gas mixture (21% Oxygen, 15% Argon, 3–5% Helium, balanced with Nitrogen) alongside an active multi-layer thermal wall. Argon acts as a molecular thermal shield that absorbs kinetic energy and halts combustion in its infancy, Helium serves as a passive "kinetic stirrer" that prevents gas stagnation and preserves normal human voice acoustics, and the heated Argon buffer wall reduces energy costs by up to 30% while rendering building facades completely non-flammable.

OFFICIAL PATENT FRAMEWORK
Status: Patent Pending

METHOD FOR PREVENTIVE THERMODYNAMIC MANAGEMENT AND HOMEOSTASIS OF A SPECIAL CASE (CLOSED ENVIRONMENT)
Author and Inventor: Milena Georgieva Zarkova

Brief Patent Definition of the General Method:
"The present invention relates to a cybernetic method for feedforward structural control of enclosed spaces. The method replaces reactive feedback systems (sensors, valves, and actuators) by pre-programming the physical and chemical constants of the environment itself in a state of rest. By introducing thermodynamically damping and kinetically balancing agents at the molecular level, the environment acquires the property of instant self-regulation, interrupting unwanted energetic chain reactions (combustion, sparking, or thermal runaway) in their infancy before reaching the critical deployment threshold, while fully preserving biological vital signs for humans."

Specific Cases of Application (Scope of Protection):

  • Case No. 1 (Astronautics and Aviation): "The Argon Loop" — a three-component gas system (Oxygen, Argon, Helium) for feedforward fire immunity and acoustic-thermal balance in spacecraft (under microgravity conditions) and aircraft.
  • Case No. 2 (Marine Industry and Submarines): Pressurized underwater vessels and deep-sea stations, where the method provides passive fire protection in enclosed compartments without oxygen loss, combined with high thermal insulation against external ocean cold.
  • Case No. 3 (Energy Facilities and Power Plants): Nuclear (NPP), thermal (TPP), and hydroelectric (HPP) power plants, electrical substations, control rooms, and cable tunnels, where the method provides continuous passive fire immunity against short circuits and overheating without power shutdown or risk to critical infrastructure.
  • Case No. 4 (Building Fire Protection and Insulation Systems): Integrated HVAC and fire protection systems for enclosed building zones with high risk or priceless contents (vaults, museums, state archives, server centers, and battery storage facilities), where extinguishing with water or chemicals is destructive. Furthermore, it applies to newly constructed or existing residential and commercial buildings as structural building elements, modular technological insulation panels for facade attachment, and/or an on-demand fire suppression system.

SCIENTIFIC-CYBERNETIC PROJECT: "THE ARGON LOOP"

Have you ever wondered how fire disappears in a dream? And then the dream itself? — natural processes.
I can tell you, if you are awake (or outside this one, inside another dream).

We have a model for everything. You know the atmosphere. And we ponder upon the dream.
So that fire-as-a-problem disappears.
And how many connections can follow after that.

Let me tell you.

The problem with fire in Space (according to publicly available information) lies in the fact that under microgravity conditions inside a spacecraft, fire is not elongated; instead, it expands into a quiet, bluish sphere. After being extinguished by NASA's reactive Feedback Loop systems, what remains is the so-called  Blind Thermal Domino. The fire consumes the oxygen around it and wraps itself in a cocoon of carbon dioxide (CO₂). The visible flame disappears, the fire looks extinguished, yet the heat remains concentrated inside this cocoon. At the micro-level, the chemical reaction continues to smolder — invisible to the human eye and sensors. Just like "the fire in a dream."

Inside this cocoon, the fire burns unseen. This invisible, concentrated thermal memory (cool flames) does not produce carbon dioxide, but generates unstable intermediate compounds (peroxides and aldehydes). They remain concentrated around the fuel source, forming an explosive chemical cloud (memory) in the stagnant air.

Under terrestrial conditions, fire needs a high temperature (above 1000°C) to sustain a chain reaction. In Space, however, there is an anomaly. The visible flame goes out, yet the chemical reaction continues at temperatures between 200°C and 300°C.
This leads to endless danger and endless calculations of reactivity.
I describe the problem because the answer is hidden within it (albeit in another dream).

Instead of worrying endlessly by building infinitely complex reactive systems, let us worry rightly. Which means focusing on the causes, not the consequences.

We all breathe air. But why does it exist in these exact proportions of constituent gases? Because this is how it maintains Earth's homeostasis and its processes. Processes in Space differ. Therefore, whatever regulates and permits a combustion process as a general constant terrestrial condition can also regulate it in Space.
In other words, if a general condition (the atmosphere) allows fire to exist, then changing that very condition holds the power to govern, regulate, and erase it.

Therein lies the key to controlling it in Space.

According to public data, the quest to control fire in spacecraft faces difficulties because it is organized around the principle:  Event (fire) — Detection (sensor) — Calculation (computer) — Action (valve). In other words, reactivity after occurrence. A classic Feedback Loop. Informational control. Slow. Unreliable in a non-linear, chaotic environment like microgravity. And carrying a high risk of failure of intermediate links (the sensors). If the sensors burn out, the system goes blind. And the problem remains.

Building homeostasis by programming the environment is a systemic method with feedforward control embedded directly into the thermodynamic field of the medium. The air itself becomes both computer and actuator simultaneously — upon crossing the critical temperature threshold, the system self-regulates at the molecular level instantaneously, eliminating the need for fragile hardware. Topological (structural) control. Putting a loop. On fire.

PHYSICAL CARRIERS of the Solution to the Fire Problem: ARGON (Ar) and HELIUM (He)

In General:
A pre-prepared mixture of  Oxygen (21%) + Argon (15%, replacing Nitrogen N₂) + Helium (3–5%, replacing Nitrogen N₂), added and proportioned to the remaining gases present in the spacecraft's atmosphere.
For thermal suffocation below the critical threshold, the percentages of Argon and Helium are indicative — a matter of precise calculation.

To accurately compute chaos at the micro-level without crashing supercomputers, a  three-step logical architecture based on the sign of variables  (+ / -) can be introduced to construct the proper proportions of the environment (the atmosphere, the mixture) — both for determining the strength of the loop itself and for Plan B in case of an emergency (such as a hull breach and depressurization of the spacecraft's atmosphere):

1. Calculating the Maximum Plus (+):
Determining the upper limit of volume — how large the flame can maximally grow over time based on the available cubic meters of air and the fuel source.

2. Dynamic Time Collision in Interrelation:
Calculating the sequence in which the expansion factor  (+) outpaces or is overtaken by the natural damping factor of suppression within the stagnant, programmed gas environment  (-).

3. Activating the Loop:
Engaging the factor pre-embedded within the conditions themselves, which reacts ahead of all others at the boundary threshold — undeniably serving both to signal a problem and to interrupt the chain reaction before the plus  (+) expands beyond the signal level (the critical thermal threshold).

Argon possesses high atomic density and low thermal conductivity (a thermal shield effect). Its massive atoms begin absorbing kinetic energy even at the low temperature of 200°C and are distributed holistically throughout the entire volume of the environment. To overcome its weight under microgravity conditions and maintain its holistic presence, Helium is added.

Argon strips away the minimal kinetic energy that sustains cool smoldering. Without this energy, the unstable intermediate compounds cannot hold together. The chain breaks physically, and the invisible cloud disintegrates before ventilation can awaken it.
That is, Argon erases the thermal memory of space once in a situation with active Cool Flames. And secondly, its action and method of suppressing fire prevent such memory from ever forming.

Put differently, Argon is a noble gas and is 100% inert, tasteless, and odorless. Stable. Lazy. Its atoms do not react with others. It can act as a thermal cage because Argon atoms surround a spark like heavy, invisible armor. They absorb the flame's thermal energy into themselves and hold it, preventing it from transferring to neighboring oxygen molecules.

It is safe for humans and surfaces because Argon's physical action is purely thermodynamic — it "soaks up" excess heat from energetic processes and halts the chain propagation of fire. At rest, it is a passive thermal insulator. Yet in the millisecond of a spark, the released heat, instead of activating an adjacent oxygen molecule (O₂) or fuel particle, strikes a heavy Argon atom, which absorbs this kinetic energy. Argon breaks the thermal bridge, the next molecule remains cold, and the flame (as if in a dream) stays isolated, loses its energetic capacity to expand, and collapses into space.

In Earth's atmosphere, Argon accounts for 0.934%. If it were higher — 10% or 20% on Earth — every time nature attempted to unleash an energetic process (lightning, wildfire, chemical reaction), the dense mass of surrounding Argon would instantly drain and tame the heat. Earth's system would be so heavily "insured" and stifled that thermal exchange would halt. The planet would cool down, and fire — the engine of human evolution and civilization — would be physically impossible to ignite outdoors.

In Space, conditions are different. On the principle that every system is a special case of organization, a spacecraft represents a special case of atmospheric organization. By artificially raising Argon to 15% (for example), we bring the planetary damping effect into the cabin to suffocate the fire's chain reaction in its infancy.

That is, on Earth we need expansion, dynamics, and movement of energy  (+), which is why Argon is kept at its safe background threshold below 1% (0.934% precisely) so as not to hinder life. In Space (inside a vessel), however, the expansion of fire is a lethal threat. There, we deliberately seek this energetic collapse for the flame.

Argon is a heavy gas. On Earth, heavy Argon has the drawback of settling on the floor. Under microgravity and weightlessness, this drawback is reduced, though not entirely. Although there is no classic terrestrial "falling" of heavy gases to the floor in microgravity, the absence of natural air convection creates a risk of diffusive passivity (stagnation). When an astronaut breathes in one spot or a machine radiates heat, the heavy, sluggish Argon atoms can cluster in local zones and form invisible "pockets" (cocoons of dense gas). Without ventilation, these heavy Argon clouds move slowly and clumsily, posing a breathing risk to the crew or uneven distribution of the loop's protective immunity.

Therefore, Helium is added. It is the second lightest element in the Universe and acts as a  "Kinetic Stirrer"because its atoms possess an exceptionally high natural rate of diffusion (thermal motion). They move rapidly, lightly, and chaotically through space, exhibiting immense kinetic energy at room temperature.

When minimally elevated Helium is added to artificially elevated Argon, the following mechanical balance triggers at the micro-level: the fast, light, and super-mobile Helium atoms constantly collide with and ricochet off the large, heavy, and "lazy" Argon atoms. With each collision, Helium transfers part of its velocity to Argon. It literally "nudges" and "stirs" the heavy Argon atoms, acting as an invisible, passive, kinetic stirrer of the medium itself. Thanks to this nudging by Helium, Argon cannot stagnate into static pockets. Helium's rapid diffusion entrains the heavy gas and distributes it holistically (uniformly) throughout the spacecraft's space.

The atmosphere itself acquires the property of a self-organizing fluid matrix. Even if the ship's artificial ventilation fails, Helium guarantees that Argon stays perfectly mixed with Oxygen and Nitrogen throughout the entire volume, ensuring equal passive immunity everywhere and protecting astronauts from breathing difficulties.
And finally, Helium helps the human voice sound normal amidst Argon's acoustic density — which is of immense daily psychological importance, as well as in moments when voice must serve as a vital tool in executing tasks.

The denser air due to Argon provides constant gentle resistance (support) to the nervous system (a sensory frame) and acts as thermal gravity — smoothly distributing heat from human bodies and machines without forming hot pockets. Solving the fire problem at its inception rather than its aftermath saves the massive costs of building reactive fire-suppression systems (cables, sensors).

Another cost-saving property of Argon is equally valuable. Because Argon has 33% lower thermal conductivity than ordinary air, it acts like a thermos and prevents heat from escaping into freezing Space. The ship's climate system can maintain a lower ambient temperature (18°C–19°C), while the free 100-watt body heat from each astronaut remains locked inside the cabin, saving heating costs.

Due to the gas's insulating properties, computers necessarily transition from unreliable air cooling to closed liquid cooling, which also serves as safer insurance for the hardware.

To save even more costs, Argon's absorbing and insulating properties can be utilized in constructing the spacecraft's outer walls on the principle of a  Multi-Layer Thermal Sandwich to protect against outer cosmic cold (around -270°C / 2.7 K), structured as follows:
Material — outer thin pocket with Krypton — material — inner wide pocket with Argon heated to a specific temperature (inexpensive, insulates intermediate temperature) — material.

How does this warmed wall pocket work? Heat always flows from warm to cold, but its rate depends on the temperature difference between the two sides of the wall. By pre-heating the inner wide Argon pocket to a level slightly above the cabin temperature (for example, 21°C inside the wall versus 19°C in the room), an active thermodynamic buffer is created. Heat from the crew and equipment has no physical reason to leave the cabin because the other side of the wall is warmer. Simultaneously, due to its high density and 33% lower thermal conductivity, the heavy and motionless Argon in microgravity acts as a thermal accumulator. It absorbs and slows down the penetration of outer cosmic cold (around -270°C) passing through the outer Krypton layer, shielding the inner hull from freezing radiation and saving heating energy.

And so on.
………

And so. Perhaps it becomes clear that:

"All that we see or seem
Is but a dream within a dream."
(Edgar Allan Poe)

Conceptually speaking — a Universe within a Universe, each founded upon the proper connection of variables.

And… perhaps, if I may, a playful riddle for the end. A puzzle.
Guess which laws of thermodynamics this text expresses?
In the following symbolic text-hint with music ( Chopin — Nocturne in C-sharp minor):

"I find no more fitting visual and auditory expression of the meaning that invisible and visible things hold as they intertwine. Heat, cold, chaos… Entropy and order. That movement of the keys between the values of good and evil, plus and minus, called melody — a path through chaos along which we walk.
Warmth in the cold.
Viewed through music and its warmth and order, certain natural laws and manifestations can be seen as remarkably wise, for they are the final emergency brake before death. A state born of a long war with many causes, many victories… and only a single defeat needed to lose it all. Saving what the pianist carries within to warm the cold is possible, yet often a difficult matter of many circumstances.
Vulnerability and fragility are constant companions of strength and warmth.
I would say, if I were the pianist today."

From "The Pianist": Chopin Nocturne C-sharp minor (Arjen Seinen — Piano).
